newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - April 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - April 17.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- The Transport Ministry has proposed fundamental restructuring of the Road Accident Fund's operations to cap loss-of-income benefits while barring accident victims from bringing civil suits for damages against wrongdoers.

- A national intelligence agent has told an inquest court that senior Inkatha Freedom Party officials were involved in "third force" activities and had strong links with former police death-squad leader Eugene de Kock.
- The central Reserve Bank has sought legislative sanction for it to have more freedom to rebut inaccurate and damaging media reports about its activities.

- The South African Railway and Harbour Workers' Union has resolved to pull out of Sun Air's restructuring committee to avoid a possible conflict of interest resulting from its investment arm's bid for a stake in the airline.
- The government has decided on a yen issue in June to kick off its four billion rand foreign borrowing programme, finance director-general Maria Ramos said.

- South Africa's largest construction and engineering group, Murray & Roberts, has settled its dispute with German-based Siemens over a 500 million rand Taiwanese train contract with M&R subsidiary Union Carriage & Wagon, the group said.
- Talks on the future of Zaire appeared to enter a crucial phase as rebel leader Laurent Kabila met President Nelson Mandela and U.N. special envoy Mohamed Sahnoun in Cape Town.
BUSINESS REPORT
- At least 20 containers of clothing and textiles, brought in duty-free under a Namibian permit, have crossed the border into South Africa, sources close to South African customs said.

- The South African Railway and Harbour Workers' Union would offer to step down from the Sun Air enterprises restructuring committee to help resolve a "conflict of interest" which was threatening to delay the airline's privatisation, a union source said.

- The Reserve Bank should soon be able to disclose the detail of "lifeboats" thrown to banks with liquidity problems, following the presentation of a bill to amend the secrecy clause in the Reserve Bank Act.
- Q Data, a computer networking equipment and services provider, saw its share price tumble 8.2 percent after the chairman, Piet den Boer, resigned unexpectedly under pressure from the board.
- The revitalisation of Permanent Bank had resulted in branch closures and more were expected, executive general manager of personal banking at Nedcor said.
SAKE-BEELD
- Piet den Boer, founder and managing director of Q Data, has been deposed by his colleagues in a palace coup.
- The government is planning new measures to save the national motor vehicle accident fund from financial disaster.
- The government is delaying an announcement on the names of the provisional candidates to buy Sun Air, because of a problem over a possible conflict of interest.
- A warning that IBM South Africa's profits were expected to show a sharp fall for the six months to end-June drove the company's share price to a new low for the year.
- The gold price fell on Wednesday afternoon to its lowest level in four years, dragging the Johannesburg Stock Exchange's gold index to its lowest over the same period.
